title: Coral and the Atlas
premise: Zephyrine Joubert, a pearl diver's child indentured to the Meridian Trading Company, has spent their whole life on a tidal island where history seems a rumor carried by ships. When the seasonal bridge closes and the company's factor is found murdered, the island becomes a sealed world of suspicion, rationed food, and old debts. Zephyrine must honor a promise made in peacetime to Captain Ilsa Voss — now declared an enemy of the crown — to smuggle her wounded son off the island before the company's private militia executes him as a spy. In the end, Zephyrine succeeds only by exposing the company's own crimes, trading their indenture for testimony, and discovering that survival bought with silence is its own kind of drowning.
about_author: Oscar Eriksen is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial trading ledgers before turning to fiction. They write about the people history recorded only as line items.
